note: Rulings for the series pages (scripts/data/build-series-early.mjs, src/lib/seriesCore.ts, series.known.test.ts). `programs`: a team id's games before a season belong to another school, so no series counts them (the exceptions are games the opponent counts, Drew's superset ruling). `drop`: a jhowell.net game whose opponent Howell joined to the wrong school. `games`: a forfeit (`w` its winner) or a vacated win (`w` null) the Wikipedia marks miss; `void: true` takes one of theirs back. `known`: a series whose rivalry-article infobox we've ruled wrong, the field, our value and why.

programs.why: Florida State College (1902–04) isn't the program FSU counts: its football starts in 1947, and Florida–Florida State starts in 1958. Wikipedia files the FSC seasons in FSU's category, and Howell's names join them to FSU.

except.why: Georgia counts the 1904 game against the Lake City school, and Florida doesn't (the infobox's per-UGA count).

programs.why: The 1904 team at Lake City (Florida Agricultural College) isn't the program UF counts, which starts in 1906 (Wikipedia's Florida category starts there). Alabama–Florida starts in 1916.

drop.why: Mississippi A&M's 5–6 loss that day was to Southwestern Presbyterian, not Southwestern Louisiana.
Tulane's 45–0 win that day was over Louisiana Normal (now Northwestern State), not Louisiana Industrial.
Cal's 67–0 win over Stanford's Student Army Training Corps team isn't counted in the Big Game series by either school.

known.title: Tennessee–Vanderbilt football rivalry
known.why: Tennessee's 2019 and 2020 wins are vacated, which the infobox's 79 Tennessee wins reflect; but its record (79–33–5) adds to 117, and with the two vacated games that's 119 of its own 120 meetings. The article's table has 34 Vanderbilt wins.

known.title: Oregon–USC football rivalry
known.why: The infobox's 65 leaves out the game whose win was vacated, which its own record notes; the page counts that game as a meeting.
